subject: Clarify: Training usage assurances and TTL for customer logs
messages:
From: Bethany Clarke <bethany@mediacorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@mediacorp.com
Date: 2026-01-15T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify: do you train on customer content?

Hi Hannah,

Quick question as we move toward a PO: can you explicitly confirm that Redwood does NOT use MediaCorp customer inputs (logs, prompts, transcripts) to train or improve any models? Procurement would like: 1) a plain-language statement we can include in our contract, 2) any supporting evidence (procedures, logs/retention controls, SOC2 snippet) and 3) the TTL you apply to runtime logs/backups (how long do copies live anywhere).

Also: are there any debug snapshots or internal telemetry that could be used for model training even if anonymized? We need specifics for our security reviewers.

Thanks — Bethany
Bethany Clarke
Sr. Security PM, MediaCorp
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Clarke <bethany@mediacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-16T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: do you train on customer content?

Hi Bethany,

Thanks for the clear list — appreciate the specificity. Short version up front: Redwood does NOT use customer runtime inputs to train or improve our public or private models. We operate a documented non-training commitment for hosted and dedicated customers; for private deployments we ship the control plane and the customer controls training settings.

I attach two short artifacts that should help procurement/security: a SOC2 summary page that points to logging/retention controls and an internal digest that explains our non-training workflows (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf; nontraining-commitment-digest.docx). Below are the specific answers you asked for.

1) Contract language (plain):
- "Redwood shall not use, access, or incorporate Customer runtime inputs (including text, prompts, transcripts, or files) to train, fine-tune, or update any models used by Redwood or third parties without the Customer's explicit written consent."

2) Evidence / procedures:
- We maintain an internal policy and operational playbook that isolates customer data streams from model training pipelines. Key controls: role-separated pipelines, tagging of production traffic, and a training-data ingest gating workflow (manual approval + audit logs).
- Audit/artifact: SOC2 control mapping for data segregation (see attached summary) and a runbook excerpt in the digest that shows how logs are scoped and how approvals are recorded.

3) TTL / retention specifics for runtime logs and snapshots:
- Short-term runtime logs (hot logs): retained for 7 days by default for debugging and metrics, then rolled to ephemeral snapshots.
- Ephemeral debug snapshots: retained up to 30 days and are periodically pruned; snapshots are not used for training.
- Long-term archival (only for customers who opt in for observability exports): retained per contract up to configured TTL, stored in a customer-controlled bucket when requested.

4) Telemetry and debug artifacts:
- Aggregated telemetry (metrics, counters) is retained for model performance monitoring and is not tied to message-level content.
- Debug snapshots that contain message-level content are strictly segregated; engineers only access them under ticketed, audited procedures and only for debugging production incidents. These artifacts are marked non-training and excluded from any training queues.

Next steps: Connor and Marissa — can you confirm the current default TTL values and where procurement should link for a signed artifact? I can add the plain contract clause to the draft PO once legal gives the green light.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Privacy & Trust, Redwood Inference
From: Bethany Clarke <bethany@mediacorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@mediacorp.com
Date: 2026-01-17T08:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: do you train on customer content?

Hi Hannah — thanks, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups from our security team:

- We need a one-page attestation letter on company letterhead that we can attach to our procurement file stating the non-training commitment and the TTLs you listed. Can you provide that?
- Procurement would like the exact S3/URI patterns or a short mapping to where runtime logs/snapshots live (even if pseudonymous) so we can map to our data flow diagrams.
- If an engineer ever needs to pull a debug snapshot containing identifiable content, will MediaCorp be notified (incidents/pull request)?

If you can get the attestation + the mapping this week we can move to PO.

Appreciate it — Bethany
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Legal Intake <legal-intake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Bethany Clarke <bethany@mediacorp.com>, procurement@mediacorp.com
Date: 2026-01-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify: do you train on customer content? — action: attestation + mapping

Forwarding to Legal / Security for action. Request from MediaCorp (external): one-page attestation on letterhead, exact storage path patterns for runtime logs/snapshots (pseudonymous OK), and confirmation on notification process for engineer access to debug snapshots.

Action items: 
- Legal: draft one-page attestation (see suggested clause below).
- Infra/Security (Connor): provide example path map (e.g., s3://redwood-prod/runtime-logs/{region}/{customer-id}/...) and confirm access audit flow.
- Privacy (Marissa): review the attestation and verify that our TTL language matches provisioning and console defaults.

Suggested attestation language (for legal to adapt):
"Redwood Inference attests that it will not use, access, or incorporate Customer runtime inputs (including text, prompts, transcripts, or files) to train, fine-tune, or update any of its models or third-party models without the Customer's explicit written consent. Runtime logs and debug artifacts are retained only as described in the attached operational summary and are excluded from training data pipelines. Access to message-level debug artifacts is logged and requires ticketed, auditable approval."

I have attached the SOC2 summary and the internal non-training digest to this thread for reference.

Hannah
